Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 2:25: Also, what I explained - that "the glorious" indicates that He is the source of the souls - is included in this: since "glorious" denotes the totality of the thirty-two paths, one of the thirty-two is the path of the creation of man, "and God created man in His image," and man is the soul, which is called "Adam," for the body is called "the flesh of man," as it is said (Exodus 30:32) "upon the flesh of man it shall not be poured."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 2:26: "And the awesome" according to this interpretation means that because of the revelation of His glory to us, we fear before Him - like the king's servants who see the king's face and fear him because he is before them, unlike one who does not see the king's face or his dwelling place, who has no fear of the king. So too our father Jacob, peace be upon him, said (Genesis 28:17) "How awesome is this place; this is none other than the house of God," for it is because it is the house of God that it inspires awe.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 2:27: Among the practices of one who fears the king is not to raise his eyes before him; so too with Moses at the vision of the burning bush, it says (Exodus 3:6) "and Moses hid his face, for he was afraid to look at God." From this it is incumbent upon a person not to walk with an upright, haughty bearing, so as not to cast off the fear [of God] from himself; and this was the excellence of Rav, peace be upon him, that one of the ten qualities he possessed was that he would not look further than four cubits, the reason being so as not to remove the fear of the Shechinah from himself, and also so as not to see any transgression [at a time when he could not prevent it, in the manner of (Psalms 119:37) "turn my eyes from seeing vanity"].
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 2:28: Particularly at the time of prayer, one must believe that His glory fills the world, and should feel awe and shame before Him and cast his eyes downward, as our Sages, of blessed memory, explained (Yevamot 105b): "One who prays must set his eyes downward and his heart upward." And let a person imagine that if he were seeing a great light so bright that it would darken his eyes, he certainly would not look directly at it; as is explained in the portion of Bereishit (4a), in the story of Rabbi Chiya, when he saw Rabbi Shimon [bar Yochai] after his passing - a voice went forth and said, "lower your eyes, do not raise your head, and do not look" - he lowered his eyes and saw a light shining afar off. Likewise, at the passing of Rashbi, peace be upon him (Ha'azinu 296b), Rabbi Abba said, "I did not raise my head, for the light was so great I could not look at it." Similarly, when a person prays and thinks that the glorious Name is before him, who is the endless source of illumination, it is fitting that he feel shame and lower his eyes before the glory of the Lord.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 2:29: Likewise, in Pirkei DeRabbi Eliezer (chapter 4), it says that the Chayot stand beside the Throne of His glory, and even though they do not know the place of His glory, nevertheless they stand in awe and fear - his words, in the fourth chapter: "And the Chayot stand beside the Throne of His glory and do not know the place of His glory, and the Chayot stand in awe and fear, trembling and quaking, and from the sweat of their faces a river of fire flows and issues forth before Him, as it is said (Daniel 7:10) 'a river of fire flowed and issued forth from before Him.' Two seraphim stand, one at the right hand of the Holy One, blessed be He, and one at His left, six wings, six wings for each - with two he covers his face so as not to look upon the face of the Shechinah," etc. - so far, as relevant to us.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 2:30: One may also explain "the glorious and the awesome" according to what is explained in the Tikkunim: just as there are thirty-two "gods" [elohim] in the account of Creation, so there are, corresponding to them, thirty-two occurrences of YHVH at known vocalizations that emerge from the verses, as is explained there; and we find in this that there is nothing in the world that is not stamped with the Name YHVH and the name Elohim together as one. If so, "the glorious" refers to the Name YHVH for the reason I explained above, and "the awesome" refers to the name Elohim, since fear mostly stems from judgment; and this is what it says (Deuteronomy 28:58) "this glorious and awesome [Name], the Lord your God" - for YHVH is "glorious" from the side of kindness, "your God" [Elohecha] from the side of judgment.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 2:31: With this we understand the verse (ibid. 4:39) "and you shall know this day and take it to your heart, that the Lord, He is God, in the heavens above," etc. The matter is that the perfection of kindness comes only when it is combined with judgment, and there is no perfection of judgment except together with mercy; and this is that YHVH, who is the master of kindness and mercy, is God [Elohim], comprising judgment; and likewise Elohim is YHVH. As for how Elohim is found within YHVH, it is explained in the Tikkunim (73b): that YHVH spelled out in full - Yud, Heh, Vav, Heh - totals [numerically] Ma"h [45], and when these letters [of the spelling] are [rearranged as] Mem, Heh, they total the numerical value of Elohim. And because the Name YHVH comprises Elohim, therefore the whole account of Creation, enacted through the thirty-two paths, came about through these two names as one; and this is [the meaning of] "that the Lord, He is God, in the heavens above" - meaning that the heavens above and the earth beneath, everything was created through Him, and there is none else.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 2:32: As for how fear results from this for a person: what we explained above in chapter one, in the name of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, peace be upon him - that the essence of fear is to fear the Name because He is great and rules, He is the root and source of all worlds, and everything is as nothing before Him - all of this our holy Torah revealed in its brief words when it said "the glorious and the awesome." "The glorious" indicates that He is great and rules, the root and source of all worlds, for through the thirty-two paths His greatness and dominion are revealed to the lower beings, and in this too He is the root and source of all worlds, for through the thirty-two paths life spreads to all the lower beings; and through the Name YHVH life spreads through all created things, which were created through Him, along the lines of His being great and ruling - so it is found that He is the root and source of all worlds.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 2:33: "And the awesome" is [the aspect of] "everything is as nothing before Him," and what was explained there at the end of chapter one concerning this matter is the fear stemming from judgment: when the Holy One, blessed be He, does good with a person, and he transgresses His will, he must fear, for the King, even though at present He does not show him an angry face, nevertheless will exact payment from him afterward; and this is [the meaning of] "your God," along the lines of what is explained in the Zohar, portion of Beshalach (51b, 60b) - I shall elaborate on this further, with the Lord's help.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 2:34: It seems to me that this fear is what Rashbi ascribed in the Zohar (Naso 122b) and in the Tikkunim (129a): the Yud of Yirah [fear] and the Heh of Ahavah [love] - and the matter of love will be explained in the next Gate, with the Lord's help. But as for ascribing fear to the Yud, which is [the aspect of] "the beginning of wisdom" [reishit chochmah], this is according to what I explained: that since "great and ruling, the root and source of all worlds," everything is found in YHVH, and the Name YHVH is in Chochmah - for the whole of the Yud is YHVH - therefore the essence of fear is there, especially when we consider what the verse says (Psalms 104:24) "You made them all with wisdom," this being the secret of Thought that sends forth life into all the worlds; and this is the verse (Proverbs 14:27) "the fear of the Lord is a source of life," as it is known that it [Chochmah/Reishit] is the source of life for all the worlds.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 2:35: Since it might seem difficult to say of Chochmah that it is the source for all the worlds, we found a proof for this in the portion of Vayikra (10b) - his words: "We learn in the Book of Enoch: at the time they showed him the wisdom of the supernal secrets, and he saw the tree of the Garden of Eden, they showed him wisdom by a supernal secret, and he saw that all the worlds were bound one to another; he asked them, upon what do they stand? They said to him, upon Yud they all stand, and from it they were built and derived, and he saw that they all tremble from fear of their Master, and by His Name they are all called" - so far. And afterward it says that the supernal thorn/point on the Yud is the fear of everything.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 2:36: Concerning the greatness of Chochmah's magnitude, it is explained in Sefer Brit Menuchah - his words: "The greatness of the host of heaven has no limit, for one angel named Uriel would traverse, in one stride, from the tenth sphere to the earth, as it is said 'now I have come.' And if such is one angel, then nine spheres are counted as almost nothing [in comparison] - how much more so Yehoel, who is above him, before whom Uriel appears as a mere youth; and Yehoel, compared to Shemuel, is as nothing; and these three princes, compared to the Da'at [Knowledge] that spreads from the products of the Intellect, are counted as nothing; and so too the Intellect compared to Binah, and Binah compared to Chochmah; and Chochmah is such that she is the mother of all the luminaries and of all the spheres and their hosts, and the luminaries that sustain their creatures, and all the treasuries are counted as nothing before her, for she lies in the bosom of the King and she manages for the King. And as the sages who plumb the depths of Chochmah, seeking to know her root, see that all the luminaries and their hosts, and the world and its hosts, and the depths, and the fish of the sea, and all the waters beneath the heavens - Chochmah hovers over them all, and none of them is visible [in comparison], and all these are counted like a small bowl with no water in it, compared to Chochmah. And when they plumbed the depths to know this great Chochmah, they said, 'How great is the Master of all the worlds, that such a light spreads forth from Him!'" - so far his words.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 2:37: Concerning this supernal fear, it is said in the Tikkunim (126b), on "and their height, and they had a height and they were awesome" [Ezekiel 1:18], regarding the letters, vowel-points, and cantillation marks, which are Binah, Chochmah, and Keter - and it says, "'and they were awesome to them' - this is the crown [Keter], where the cantillation marks are" - so far his words.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 2:38: Because this fear is in a hidden place, it is written afterward (Deuteronomy 28:59) "and the Lord will make your plagues wondrous [pil'i]" - and it is known that the term "wonder" [pele] applies only to this place, as is explained in the Zohar, portion of Tzav (31a), on the verse (Isaiah 9:5) "Pele Yoetz [Wonderful Counselor]."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 2:39: Concerning this fear it is said (Proverbs 10:27) "the fear of the Lord [YHVH] adds days" - this being the fear that stems from the Name YHVH, as we explained in the four aspects concerning fear, all of which depend on YHVH, "great and ruling, the root and source," etc., and "everything is as nothing before Him." Above [in Chochmah] is the place of the addition of life, as is explained in the Zohar (Tosefot, Noach 69b), on the verse (Isaiah 38:5) "behold, I will add to your days." Therefore it does not say "the fear of Elohim adds days," for the fear of Elohim is fear from judgment, and it is a place of diminishment and constriction, and is not on the level of the fear that is significant enough to add days. But this fear [of YHVH] is fear stemming from His greatness, blessed be He, on account of YHVH, for this Name gave him existence in his two hundred and forty-eight limbs and his soul, and is imprinted within him in every limb; and he fears to sin before the King who is before him, like the king's servants, who, seeing the king's seal, fear that seal as though it were the king himself, as is explained in the Tikkunim (65b) on the verse (Song of Songs 8:6) "set me as a seal."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 2:40: We find, then, three aspects in the verse: the first, the fear of Elohim, does not add days, but only [preserves] the days allotted to him from the day of his creation, which stand for him [as they are]. And the highest degree among the levels is the fear of YHVH, which adds days. And "the years of the wicked," who have no fear at all, "shall be shortened" (Proverbs 10:27) from the days allotted to them.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 2:41: Further, one can give a fourth interpretation of "the glorious and the awesome," along the lines explained in Ra'aya Meheimna (portion of Kedoshim, 82a) regarding "honor your father and your mother." There it is explained that Chochmah is called "glory" [kavod] because she is a throne for the supernal crown, to serve beneath it and to carry out its utterance through her thirty-two paths - his words, briefly: "and because she carries out His utterance and command without delay, through the thirty-two paths by which the whole account of Creation was created, she is called 'glory,' as in 'and in His Temple all say Glory' (Psalms 29:9)," etc. - so far, as relevant to us.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 2:42: Further, there, a bit later, concerning the honor of father and mother: the honor of one's father and mother is to carry out their command, and their command is [analogous to] the positive commandments; and our Sages, masters of the Mishnah, have established that there is one who is commanded and performs, and therefore it [Chochmah] is [called] "we will do and we will hear" - and this is the "glory" of Father and Mother, who commanded their child to do thus, and he does it immediately without any delay at all - so far. And it is explained there further, that "every man shall fear his mother and father" - this fear is to be careful not to transgress a negative commandment.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 2:43: Along these lines we may explain "the glorious and the awesome": "the glorious" - that all created beings are subject to His utterance, to honor Him and do His will; "the awesome" - that all fear not to transgress His commandments, as the prophet said (Jeremiah 5:22) "Will you not fear Me, says the Lord, will you not tremble before Me, who has placed the sand as a boundary for the sea, an eternal decree that it cannot pass," etc. This verse will be explained, with the Lord's help, in the next chapter.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 2:44: One may also offer a further gloss based on what is explained in the Tikkunim (5a): that the Name YHVH comprises both the negative and positive commandments - "Shin-Mem" [365, the negative commandments] together with "Yud-Heh" totals 365 [i.e., the numerical association], "Zayin-Kaf-Reish-Yud" [248, the positive commandments] together with "Vav-Heh" totals 248. If so, we find that YHVH is called both "glorious" and "awesome" - "glorious" in that He is the source of the positive commandments in the secret of Vav-Heh, and "awesome" from the side of the negative commandments, which are Yud-Heh.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 3:1: Since our discussion in the previous chapter preceded regarding "the glorious and the awesome" - that among the particulars of fear is that since all created beings are subject to His utterance and fear not to transgress His command, so too must a person fear and feel shame not to transgress the commandment of his Maker, and this is the level of fear that comes from shame - we saw fit to append this chapter, to expand on the matter with the words of our Sages, of blessed memory.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 3:2: Our Sages, of blessed memory, said (Sifrei, portion of Ha'azinu) - their words: "'Give ear, O heavens' - the Holy One, blessed be He, said to Moses: tell Israel, look at the heavens which I created to serve you; have they perhaps changed their custom, or has the solar sphere perhaps gone out in the west, as it is said (Ecclesiastes 1:5) 'and the sun rises and the sun sets'? Not only that, but it rejoices to do My will, as it is said (Psalms 19:6) 'and he is like a bridegroom coming forth from his chamber.' 'And let the earth hear the words of my mouth' - look at the earth which I created to serve you; has it perhaps changed its custom, has it perhaps happened that you sowed and it did not sprout, or that you sowed wheat and it brought forth barley, or has this cow ever said, I will not thresh and I will not plow, or has this donkey ever said, I will not carry and I will not go? And likewise concerning the sea it says (Jeremiah 5:22) 'Will you not fear Me, says the Lord, will you not tremble before Me, who has placed the sand as a boundary for the sea' - from the time I decreed upon it, has it perhaps changed its custom and said, I will rise up and flood the world, as it is said (Job 38:10-11) 'and I broke for it My decree... and said, thus far you shall come and no further'? Not only that, but it grieves and cannot do it, as it is said (Jeremiah 5:22) 'and they toss but they cannot [prevail].' And is this not an argument from minor to major: if these, who were made neither for reward nor for punishment - if they merit, they receive no reward, and if they sin, they receive no punishment, and they have no pity on their sons and daughters - have not changed their custom, how much more so must you, who if you merit, receive reward, and if you sin, receive punishment, and you have pity on your sons and daughters - how much more must you take care not to change your ways" - so far, as relevant to us.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 3:3: The pious master, author of Chovot HaLevavot (Gate of Self-Reckoning, chapter 3), wrote something relevant to this; I have chosen to quote part of his words - his words: "And the sixth [reckoning]: that a person consider within himself, when he senses that his character traits are inclining him to defy the Creator and to break His covenant, and let him reflect within himself and bring before his heart all that he has grasped with his senses of the roots and branches of the world, its simple and composite elements, its upper and lower realms - that everything stands by His word and keeps the covenant of the [Divine] Name. Has he seen anything from it emerge from the bond of the service of God, blessed be He, or defy His word and break His covenant? And let him consider man's own limbs: were they to transgress God's covenant within man, his natural limbs that are supposed to move would rest, or those that are supposed to rest would move; or if the senses did not convey to him what they were commanded to convey to him, his constitution would be ruined, his composition disordered, and his governance annulled. How, then, should a man not feel ashamed to transgress the covenant of his God in a world where [even the elements] do not transgress the covenant of their God - in himself and in the helpers who are obligated in His service and bear his condition, namely his limbs? Do you not know that God stipulated in His faithful Torah that everything in the world would be at your disposal and by your desire if you serve Him, and that it would turn away from your desire when you transgress His word, as is explained in the portion 'if you walk in My statutes'?" - so far his words. I have abbreviated part of his wording so as not to lengthen it.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 3:4: Now in this manner one may also explain the verse (Jeremiah 5:22) "Will you not fear Me, says the Lord, will you not tremble before Me, who has placed the sand as a boundary for the sea," etc.: since the sea is a physical thing without sensation, and how much more so the other created things that do the will of the Creator, blessed be He, how should a person not fear to transgress the will of his Creator with his limbs, which were created to serve the Creator? For the heart is the principal organ created to fear the Creator, since fear resides in the heart, as it is said (Jeremiah 32:40) "and I will put My fear in their hearts," and further on the prophet says (ibid. 5:24) "and they did not say in their hearts, let us fear the Lord," etc. - and yet it was precisely there [in the heart] that the will of the Creator was transgressed, as it is said (ibid. 5:23) "but this people has a stubborn and rebellious heart," etc. - how much more so the other limbs, through which the will of the Creator was certainly transgressed.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 3:5: I have seen fit to examine these verses closely and explain them, with God's help, since they pertain to the matter of the fear of the Lord. First, one should note the seeming repetition in the verse "Will you not fear Me, says the Lord, will you not tremble before Me" - it seems the same idea is repeated in different words. And what does "Me" [Oti] mean, and afterward "before Me" [mipanai], as though they were the same thing? And afterward it goes on to say "and they did not say in their hearts, let us fear the Lord," etc. - what is the point of this second [mention of] fear? Why not combine them and teach them together, saying simply "Will you not fear Me... who has placed the sand as a boundary for the sea... and gives you the early and late rain in its season," etc.? Furthermore, above, in the first verse, fear is mentioned without qualification, "Will you not fear Me," without mentioning the heart, while in the second [mention of] fear, the heart is mentioned - we must understand the reason for this.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 3:6: To answer in general why two [mentions of] fear are stated, one may say that the first fear corresponds to the negative commandments, as the plain sense of the verse itself demonstrates, saying "will you not tremble before Me, who has placed the sand as a boundary for the sea... that it cannot pass," etc., "and you are passing beyond the boundary of the Torah," as it says "but this people has a stubborn and rebellious heart," etc. And the second fear corresponds to the positive commandments, that one must fear and say in his heart: since the Holy One, blessed be He, does good with us, giving early and late rain and the appointed weeks of the harvest, so too we must take care to perform every commandment in its proper time, as we were commanded, for through this we grant strength above, as in (Deuteronomy 33:26) "who rides the heavens to help you" - and the opposite, God forbid (ibid. 32:18) "the Rock who bore you, you have forgotten," [taken as "you have weakened"] as our Sages, of blessed memory, explained in the Pesikta, quoted in the Yalkut, on the verse "the Rock that bore you, you have weakened" - their words: "When Israel does the will of the Omnipresent, they add strength and might, as is said (Numbers 14:17) 'and now, let the power of the Lord be great,' and when they anger Him, as it were, 'the Rock that bore you, you have weakened'" - so far, as relevant to us; and they elaborate further there.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 3:7: With this we also explain why the heart is not mentioned in the first fear: because that fear is not in the heart alone, but rather encompasses all the limbs of a person, which transgress the whole Torah - for each and every limb must fear not to transgress the commandment that depends on that limb, just as the sea keeps its statute not to transgress, as is explained in Chovot HaLevavot. But the second fear, which pertains to the positive commandments, depends on the heart, for it consists of a person examining, in his heart, the good the Creator has done for him, as we have explained.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 3:8: And on this note, regarding the fear that is in the heart, it is known what is explained in the Tikkunim (24a), that "heart" [lev] unqualified refers to the heart that "understands from the heart," etc., meaning that "fear enters into his heart," which is the secret of the Heh-Yud of Elohim; and "fear" unqualified, which encompasses the negative commandments, is the lower fear. This is what appears to me.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 3:9: Regarding the repetition in the verse "Will you not fear Me, says the Lord, will you not tremble before Me": the explanation is that "will you not fear Me" refers to His own essence, which is hidden and beyond our grasp; "says the Lord" - this Name, YHVH, is called "He, blessed be He," from the aspect that He brought all beings into existence, and the beings He created point to His greatness and that He, blessed be He, created them, as was explained in chapter one. "Will you not tremble before Me" [mipanai] means from the aspect of His "face" that is revealed to you - like the parable of one who hears news of the king, or one who sees his face; for one who sees his face fears the king even more and trembling seizes him as a woman in labor, and this is [the meaning of] "will you not tremble before Me."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 3:10: These two aspects are both present in the sea, and both are present in man. As for the sea, it is already known, as explained in our passage quoted at the beginning of this chapter, that the Holy One, blessed be He, decreed upon it not to go beyond its boundary, and the sand is its boundary; and the King's decree, made at the time of the world's creation, is a hidden aspect, while the sea's keeping of the King's command, which He commanded it so many years ago, even though the King is not now commanding it anything - this is the aspect of "will you not fear Me." And corresponding to "before Me" is that the sea sees the sand around it and knows that the Holy One, blessed be He, placed this boundary for it, and does not transgress it.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 3:11: Corresponding to these two aspects mentioned, there is a parallel in man regarding the Torah: the Torah and commandments given to us in the Five Books of the Torah are the boundary we perpetually see, like the sand that surrounds the sea; and this, in truth, is the King's face - except that we do not actually see the King's face, but the Torah is the stamped image of the King. But we did see the King Himself at the time of the giving of the Torah, as we explained in chapter one, and this is [the meaning of] "will you not fear Me" - for it should be fitting that the first command from the King Himself should suffice for us, along with the boundary He set for us afterward in the matter of the commandments - just as the sea was commanded only once, and upon that single command it stands, heeding its warning.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 3:12: It may also be said that the boundary the Holy One, blessed be He, created within man himself is the good inclination [yetzer tov]; this is what our Sages, of blessed memory, explained, that there are two chambers in the heart, one full of blood, which is the dwelling place of the evil inclination, and the other, a chamber without blood, the dwelling place of the good inclination. Now, when the evil inclination rages, urging one to transgress the Torah, the good inclination stands opposite it, counseling it to return to the good; and there is no wicked person to whom thoughts of repentance do not come before he commits the transgression - only that his inclination seduces him, and afterward he regrets it. Thus it is said (Akeidat Yitzchak, Gate 67) "the wicked are full of regrets," and therefore the verse says (Jeremiah 5:23) "but this people has a stubborn and rebellious heart; they have turned aside and gone," for they turned aside from the boundary within their heart, which is the good inclination warning them, and they went outside [that boundary]. This is what our Sages, of blessed memory, said in the first chapter of Bava Batra (16a): "I created the evil inclination, I created the good inclination; I created the evil inclination, I created a remedy against it, which is the Torah."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 3:13: On this note, one may find an allusion in the repetition of the verse: "Will you not fear Me, says the Lord" corresponds to the Name YHVH; "will you not tremble before Me" [mipanai] corresponds to the name Adonai, which denotes "face" [panim], and this is the secret of "the whole earth is full of His glory," as is explained in the Tikkunim. Corresponding to these two aspects in the sea: the one corresponding to the name Adonai is "the sand, a boundary for the sea, an eternal decree that it cannot pass" - this being the revealed aspect. And corresponding to the hidden aspect is (Jeremiah 5:22) "and they toss but they cannot [prevail]; its waves roar but cannot pass it" - and at first glance "and they toss but they cannot" seems superfluous. But the matter can be understood from what is explained (Noach 69b) on the verse (Psalms 89:10) "You rule the pride of the sea; when its waves rise, You still them" - for when the sea is in the height of its raging, a thread of kindness is drawn into it to calm it from its fury and rage; and so it says there, "You still them" - "You break them, to return them to their place" - and because it is the Holy One, blessed be He, who sends forth this thread, it is therefore ascribed to the Name YHVH.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 3:14: With this we understand the passage from the Sifrei that we quoted at the beginning of the chapter, which said, "not only that, but it grieves and cannot do it, as it is said, 'and they toss but they cannot.'"
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 3:15: Corresponding to these two aspects explained, there is a parallel in man: the first is the inner aspect of the spirit within him, which is the secret of "He who forms the spirit of man within him" (Zechariah 12:1), as is explained in the Zohar (Mikeitz 197a); and the second is the aspect of the garment, which is the body, in which the spirit is clothed. And when a person considers that his spirit and all his limbs are made and directed by the counsel of the Supernal court, he must fear lest he blemish his limbs or his spirit, as our Sages, of blessed memory, explained on the verse (Ecclesiastes 2:12) "that which they have already made" - their words: "'that which they have already made' - it is not written 'made him' but 'made him' [in the plural form implying multiple makers] - as it were, the King of kings of kings and His court took a count of your every limb and established you on your foundation, as it is said (Deuteronomy 32:6) 'He made you and established you'" - so far, quoted in the Yalkut on Job (remez 914), on the verse (Job 26:13) "by His spirit the heavens were made fair," etc. Thus has been explained one aspect of the fear that comes from shame.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 3:16: Further, a second aspect: when the Holy One, blessed be He, grants a person wealth, honor, possessions, children, and the like goods of this world, he must fear lest sin be the cause [of losing them], as is said of our father Jacob, peace be upon him (Genesis 32:8) "and Jacob was greatly afraid," and our Sages, of blessed memory, explained (Berachot 4a) that he feared lest sin be the cause - for Rabbi Yaakov bar Idi raised a contradiction: it is written "and behold I am with you and will keep you wherever you go," and it is written "and Jacob was greatly afraid"; he said, he feared lest sin be the cause, as is taught: "'until Your people pass over, O Lord' (Exodus 15:16) - this refers to the first entry [into the Land, under Joshua]; 'until the people whom You have acquired pass over' - this refers to the second entry [in the days of Ezra]." From this our Sages said: Israel deserved to have a miracle performed for them in the days of Ezra just as was done for them in the days of Joshua, but sin was the cause [that prevented it] - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 3:17: Know that this fear we explained, "lest sin be the cause," concerns the blemish to the attribute [the Shechinah] that accompanies us in exile, and for this reason he brought proof from the beraita that in the days of Ezra sin was the cause; and the cause of that sin was that they became blemished through foreign women, and for this reason he brought this beraita, to teach us the secret of where sin's causing [of harm] blemishes, as Rashbi explains in the portion of Ki Tisa (Zohar 194b). And the matter of how sin blemishes here is explained by Rashbi in the portion of Vayikra (20a), on the verse (Psalms 32:5) "I acknowledged my sin to You."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 3:18: With this we understand the fear of "lest sin be the cause," as Rashbi explains in the portion of Bereishit (ibid. 12a) - his words: "Rabbi Elazar said, one need never forget fear in any commandment, and how much more so in this commandment must fear be needed to cling to it. How does one cling to it? Love is on the one, good side - as it is said, that it gives wealth and goodness, length of days, children, and sustenance; then fear must be aroused, to fear lest one cause sin, and of this it is written (Proverbs 28:14) 'happy is the man who fears always,' because fear is included within love. And so it must be aroused on the other side, of harsh judgment: when one sees harsh judgment resting upon him, then fear should be aroused, and he should fear his Master as is fitting, and not harden his heart, and of this it is written 'but he who hardens his heart shall fall into evil' - into that other side which is called 'evil.' Thus fear is found bound to both sides and comprised of them, and this is complete love, as is fitting" - so far his words.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 3:19: Now, what he said, "one need never forget fear," etc., was explained above on the previous page, that it says "Bereishit," in which "fear" is alluded to, this being the gateway and portal to all the commandments; and he says that fear is "lest one cause sin" - this is the secret I have alluded to.
